title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the bracketed general discussion from p.534 (archive 462) on sections of the extension M_{ρ,σ} → T_{ρ,σ}, whose kernel is G^+_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG. It then treats the first of three explicit subgroups.

General set-up. Use the presentation M_{ρ,σ} ≅ (R_{ρ,σ} × SG)/μ_2, with μ_2 embedded diagonally (made explicit on the next page, formula (9)).
- A section of M over T is the same as a homomorphism ψ: R_{ρ,σ} → M_{ρ,σ} lifting the epimorphism R → T and trivial on its kernel.
- On the product extension such a ψ can be written x ↦ ψ(x) = x·ψ°(x) (formula (5)), with ψ°: R_{ρ,σ} → SG a homomorphism.
- Descending through the diagonal μ_2, condition (3) becomes (6): ψ°(x) = x on μ_2 = R_{ρ,σ} ∩ SG.

So sections of M over T correspond bijectively to homomorphisms R_{ρ,σ} → SG that restrict to the identity on the common central μ_2. This is the standard description of splittings of a central pushout/quotient extension. The three subgroups M(0), M(1/2), M(−j) will give pairs (ψ_0, ψ°_0), (ψ_{1/2}, ψ°_{1/2}), (ψ_{−j}, ψ°_{−j}).

Case 1°, M_{ρ,σ}(0).
- In the notation of p.529 it consists of elements satisfying one of the equivalent conditions (7): y = y_1, f = 1, u ∈ ΓT_0, α_0 = α, β_0 = β.
- Hence (8): M(0) = Θ^{-1}(T_0). Here Θ: M_{ρ,σ} → G is the homomorphism from the description of p.526 ff., and T_0 ⊂ G is a one-dimensional torus with det|T_0: T_0 ≅ G_m.
- Θ restricted to G^+ = SG is the canonical inclusion SG ↪ G, and SG ∩ T_0 = {1} because det is injective on T_0. So M(0) ∩ G^+ = (Θ|SG)^{-1}(T_0) = {1}, and M(0) → T is a monomorphism.
- It remains to show surjectivity onto T. The next page does this by computing the corresponding ψ°_0(r) = κ(r)^{-1}·i_{T_0}(κ(r)^2), where κ = Θ|R: R → G_m is scalar, and checking it is the identity on μ_2.

The overall purpose is a case-by-case construction of distinguished partial or total sections (sub-group-sections) of an auxiliary extension M_{ρ,σ}. These appear to serve the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' in the second part of the Longue Marche. The likely setting is group(-scheme)s attached to GL_2-type data acting on fundamental groupoids/Teichmüller tower relations, but the exact meaning of ρ, σ, R, T cannot be determined from this page.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The verification M(0) ∩ SG = SG ∩ T_0 = {1} is correct, given that det|T_0 is an isomorphism.
Gap: the cited monomorphism criterion '(x)' is an unreadable reference. Surjectivity of M(0) → T is left to the next page.
On the next page, the check that ψ°_0 is the identity on μ_2 is written sloppily ('κ(r)^{-1} = κ(r) = r'). It is fine, since κ(r) = r for r ∈ μ_2 scalar and κ(r)^2 = 1.

ideas.what: Sections of an extension of the form (R × SG)/μ_2 → T correspond to homomorphisms ψ°: R → SG that are the identity on the diagonal μ_2
ideas.modern_name: classification of splittings of a central quotient/pushout extension

ideas.what: A subgroup Θ^{-1}(T_0) is a section subgroup: it meets the kernel trivially because SG ∩ T_0 = 1 (det injective on T_0)
ideas.modern_name: complement to a normal subgroup / torus transversal to SL

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification step within a long computational section of the unpublished 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The group theory is standard, and the specific objects M_{ρ,σ} are only of interest within the larger, unpublished context.

(6) reads 'Ψ°(x) = x sur μ_2 = R_{ρ,σ} ∩ SG' (no extra subscript ∘ on Ψ°).
The overbrace label above the intersection is '(Θ|SG)^{-1}(T_0)'.
'(qui est mono par (x))': the reference is likely '(α)' or a formula label, not literally '(x)'.
